questions.q: State the triangle law of vector addition in your own words and draw a labelled diagram showing vectors \(\vec{a}\), \(\vec{b}\), and their resultant \(\vec{a}+\vec{b}\).
questions.a: The triangle law: if \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\) are represented by two sides of a triangle taken in order (tail of \(\vec{b}\) at head of \(\vec{a}\)), then the third side taken in the reverse order (from tail of \(\vec{a}\) to head of \(\vec{b}\)) represents \(\vec{a}+\vec{b}\). A wrong answer where the student draws \(\vec{b}\) starting from the tail of \(\vec{a}\) (tail-to-tail) reveals confusion between triangle law and parallelogram law. If they draw the resultant from head of \(\vec{a}\) to tail of \(\vec{b}\), they have reversed the order.

questions.q: Explain why the triangle law and parallelogram law of vector addition always give the same resultant vector. Use a diagram in your explanation.
questions.a: In the parallelogram construction, the diagonal from the common point O to the opposite vertex is exactly the third side of the triangle formed by \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\) placed head-to-tail (since opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal and parallel). A wrong answer that merely states “they are equivalent” without referencing the geometric construction (e.g., \(\vec{b}\) in parallelogram is parallel to \(\vec{b}\) in triangle) shows the student has memorized the fact but not understood the proof. If they claim the other diagonal is the resultant, they confuse the direction of the sum.

questions.q: Two forces \(\vec{F_1}\) and \(\vec{F_2}\) of magnitudes 6 N and 8 N act at a point with an angle of 60° between them. Find the magnitude of the resultant force using the parallelogram law formula.
questions.a: Magnitude \(R = \sqrt{6^2+8^2+2\cdot6\cdot8\cos60°} = \sqrt{36+64+48} = \sqrt{148} = 2\sqrt{37} \approx 12.17\) N. A common error: using \(\cos60°=0.5\) but forgetting the factor 2, giving \(\sqrt{36+64+24}=\sqrt{124}\) (wrong). Another error: using \(\sin60°\) instead of \(\cos60°\), which would be the formula for the magnitude of the cross product, not the sum.

questions.q: Compare the magnitude and direction of the resultant when two vectors of fixed magnitudes \(a\) and \(b\) are added at angles \(\theta = 0°, 90°, 180°\). What pattern do you observe?
questions.a: At \(\theta=0°\): \(R = a+b\) (max), direction same as both. At \(\theta=90°\): \(R = \sqrt{a^2+b^2}\), direction at \(\tan\phi = b/a\). At \(\theta=180°\): \(R = |a-b|\) (min), direction of the larger vector. The pattern: \(R\) decreases monotonically from \(a+b\) to \(|a-b|\) as \(\theta\) goes from 0 to \(\pi\). A wrong answer that says \(R\) is constant or increases with \(\theta\) reveals a fundamental misunderstanding of the cosine term’s effect. If they say direction is always the angle bisector, they incorrectly assume equal magnitudes.

questions.q: A student adds two vectors of magnitudes 5 m and 12 m by simply writing “5 + 12 = 17 m” as the resultant magnitude. Identify the error and give the correct range of possible resultant magnitudes.
questions.a: The error is treating vectors as scalars; vector addition depends on the angle \(\theta\). The resultant magnitude can range from \(|12-5|=7\) m (opposite directions) to \(12+5=17\) m (same direction). A wrong answer that says the resultant is always 17 m shows the student ignores direction entirely. If they say the range is 0 to 17 m, they forget vectors cannot cancel completely unless magnitudes are equal.

questions.q: Create a real-life problem (Indian context) involving addition of two vectors where the angle between them is not 0° or 90°. Provide the full solution using both triangle and parallelogram laws.
questions.a: Example: A cyclist rides 3 km east, then turns 30° north of east and rides 4 km. Find the displacement from start. Solution: Use triangle law: draw 3 km east, then 4 km at 30° from east. Resultant magnitude \(R = \sqrt{3^2+4^2+2\cdot3\cdot4\cos30°} = \sqrt{9+16+12\sqrt{3}} \approx 6.77\) km. Direction \(\tan\phi = \frac{4\sin30°}{3+4\cos30°} = \frac{2}{3+2\sqrt{3}} \approx 0.309\), \(\phi \approx 17.2°\) north of east. Parallelogram law gives the same. A poor answer would omit the diagram, use wrong angle, or add magnitudes directly.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The triangle law of vector addition states that if two vectors are represented as two sides of a triangle taken in order, their sum (______) is represented by the third side taken in the reverse order.
Fill in the blank: Imagine a boat crossing a river: the boat’s engine gives it a velocity of 10 km/h ______ to the bank, while the river current adds a velocity of 5 km/h parallel to the bank.
